feed.title: Siegu blog — notes from building a private photo library
feed.subtitle: Thoughts on building a private, local-first photo library: why private by design beats a privacy policy, how on-device AI works, and more from the Siegu project.

entry.title: Why “private by design” beats a privacy policy
entry.summary: Every photo service has a privacy policy. And every one of them can upload your photos. A policy just describes what a company may legally do with your data — it doesn't prevent anything. Private by design means there is nothing to prevent, because there's nothing to take. Siegu runs its whole pipeline — indexing, search, face recognition, captions — on your own hardware. The “cloud” isn't where features live; it's what we avoid. That's a small difference in marketing and a huge difference in where your memories end up.

entry.title: How a search engine for one person works
entry.summary: Semantic search usually means uploading your library so a server can index it. Siegu does the same job with CLIP running locally through ONNX Runtime: describe a photo (“sunsets at the beach”) and it's found on your drive, not a data center. Local AI is slower per query than a warehouse of GPUs, so the app indexes in the background and answers from a pre-computed index. You get the magic without shipping your memories anywhere.
